title: The quotient by the I-power torsion submodule has no I-torsion (I finitely generated)
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $I\subseteq R$ a finitely generated ideal and $M$ an $R$-module. Put $M[I^\infty]=\{m\in M:\ I^nm=0\text{ for some }n\ge1\}$, a submodule of $M$, and $M'=M/M[I^\infty]$. Then $M'[I]=0$: if $\bar x\in M'$ satisfies $a\bar x=0$ for every $a\in I$, then $\bar x=0$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 05EB (lemma-divide-by-torsion, line 24042), part (1)

proof.text: Write $T=M[I^\infty]$. This is a submodule: $0\in T$; if $I^pm=0$ and $I^qn=0$, then $I^{\max(p,q)}(m+n)=0$; and if $r\in R$, then $I^p(rm)=rI^pm=0$. For $x\in M$ let $\bar x$ be its class in $M/T$. The condition $I\bar x=0$ means precisely that $ax\in T$ for every $a\in I$, since the kernel of $M\to M/T$ is $T$.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 05EB (lemma-divide-by-torsion), lines 24042-24063, opening sentence; submodule and quotient details expanded

proof.text: Choose generators $I=(f_1,\dots,f_t)$. For each $j$ the element $f_jx$ lies in $T$ by step 1, so choose an integer $n_j\ge1$ with $I^{n_j}f_jx=0$. If $t=0$, then $I=0$, so $T=M$ because $I^1M=0$ and $\bar x=0$. Henceforth suppose $t>0$ and put $N=2+\sum_{j=1}^t n_j$.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 05EB (lemma-divide-by-torsion), lines 24053-24059: finite generators, individual annihilating powers, and the common exponent

proof.text: The ideal $I^N$ is generated by monomials $f_1^{e_1}\cdots f_t^{e_t}$ with nonnegative exponents summing to $N$. For each such monomial some $j$ has $e_j\ge n_j+1$: otherwise $\sum e_j\le\sum n_j<N$. Factor that monomial as $f_j$ times a product of $N-1$ generators, including at least $n_j$ further copies of $f_j$. That latter product lies in $I^{n_j}$, so its product with $f_jx$ is zero by step 2. Every generating monomial of $I^N$ therefore kills $x$, and $I^Nx=0$.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 05EB (lemma-divide-by-torsion), lines 24057-24060: the statement 'Thus I^N m=0' expanded into the monomial and pigeonhole calculation

proof.text: For $t>0$, step 3 says $x\in T=M[I^\infty]$, so $\bar x=0$ in $M/T$. The $t=0$ case was settled in step 2. Thus every class annihilated by $I$ is zero, equivalently $(M/M[I^\infty])[I]=0$.
